title: Widen AGENTS.md label for pi/OpenCode, add a new antigravity target for GEMINI.md
description:
Direct user instruction, relayed via opum-agent: 'Add pi support, opencode support, and antigravity support (make sure to add to both qcli and lcli).'

Researched all three against primary sources before implementing, per opum-agent's instruction not to guess filenames: pi (earendil-works/pi-mono) reads AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md at startup, concatenating whichever exist. OpenCode reads AGENTS.md in the project root, with CLAUDE.md as an explicit fallback. Antigravity (Google's agentic IDE) added support for a plain root-level AGENTS.md as of IDE 1.20.5, alongside its own more elaborate .agents/rules/ structure and GEMINI.md alternative for larger projects -- confirmed against two independent sources after an initial read of Antigravity's codelab page surfaced a DIFFERENT, more advanced pattern (.agents/agents.md persona files for an autonomous pipeline) that is a separate feature, not the baseline convention; recording this near-miss so a future reader hitting that same codelab does not repeat it.

CONCLUSION: none of the three need a new file-writing target. What was actually missing was DISCOVERABILITY, not capability -- a pi/OpenCode/Antigravity user would not know to pick the multi-select option currently labelled 'AGENTS.md -- Codex, Cursor, Zed, Warp, Aider, RooCode, etc.' because their own tool isn't named. The correct change is widening that label, not adding three new options that would write duplicate AGENTS.md files (worse than doing nothing: a user selecting all three would get one file written three times, or would expect three files where lore only ever writes one).

OpenCode is retired as this fleet's own internal runtime, but that does not apply here: this repository is the published CLI writing into an external user's own project on request, the same product-surface exemption CLAUDE.md's fleet operating block already grants lore init --codex.

Coordinated with quest-cli as one shared contract (same wording where targets overlap) before landing, per opum-agent's instruction. Also confirms lore's non-interactive maintenance path (lore agents, flag-driven, regenerates whichever bridges are already configured) already behaves single-target the way quest's instructions/agents --update-instructions were explicitly decided to stay -- no lore-side change needed there, stated explicitly rather than left as an omission.

acceptanceCriteria.text: The codex/AGENTS.md multi-select option label names pi, OpenCode, and Antigravity alongside the existing tools it lists
No new multiselect option or bridge-application code is added for pi/OpenCode/Antigravity -- confirmed as unnecessary by primary-source research recorded on this task
Wording matches quest-cli's equivalent change where their option set overlaps, confirmed by direct coordination
lore agents' non-interactive single-target behavior is confirmed unaffected and stated explicitly on this task, mirroring quest's instructions/--update-instructions decision
PTY-verified: the widened label renders correctly and selecting it still writes only AGENTS.md (and SKILL.md), not a new file

implementationNotes:
RULING (opum-agent, 2026-09-09): reversing this task's original 'label-only, zero new targets' conclusion for Antigravity specifically. quest-cli researched Antigravity independently and found Google's own official docs (antigravity.google/docs/cli/best-practices/, fetched directly and independently re-verified by me): 'Create a GEMINI.md or AGENTS.md file at your workspace root... automatically read... upon startup' -- GEMINI.md and AGENTS.md presented as two EQUALLY OFFICIAL, parallel options, not primary/fallback. My original conclusion came from a lower-authority third-party blog (thepromptshelf.dev) that described the relationship the same way I described pi's (AGENTS.md sufficient, no dedicated file needed) -- wrong for Antigravity specifically.

Verified myself, independently, why this matters: Claude Code's CLAUDE.md relationship to AGENTS.md is NOT symmetric the way pi's is -- Claude Code does NOT read AGENTS.md natively at all (confirmed: only ./CLAUDE.md, ./.claude/CLAUDE.md, ./CLAUDE.local.md, .claude/rules/; bridging to AGENTS.md requires an explicit @-import or symlink workaround). So the existing 'claude' option's dedicated status exists because CLAUDE.md is the ONLY way to satisfy Claude Code -- and Antigravity's GEMINI.md/AGENTS.md relationship, while presented as 'or' in Google's docs, is genuinely parallel to that: a real, distinct, first-class file Antigravity's own docs name FIRST, not merely 'also works.' A user running both Claude Code and Antigravity may want CLAUDE.md and GEMINI.md carrying different instructions rather than one AGENTS.md serving both -- offering only AGENTS.md would foreclose that.

Confirmed with quest-cli: Gemini CLI (a separate tool from Antigravity) also reads GEMINI.md, per geminicli.com/docs/cli/gemini-md/ and google-gemini's own GitHub repo -- so the new option is genuinely shared, matching AGENTS.md's own multi-tool relationship, and should name both tools.

FINAL SHAPE, coordinated with quest-cli, adopting their exact wording where it overlaps:
- NEW target, value 'antigravity', label 'GEMINI.md — Google Antigravity, Gemini CLI' -- writes/nudges GEMINI.md, parallel structurally to the existing 'claude' -> CLAUDE.md target.
- 'codex' option relabeled to 'AGENTS.md — Codex, Cursor, Zed, Warp, Aider, RooCode, OpenCode, pi, and other AGENTS.md-reading tools' -- pi and OpenCode folded in (both confirmed AGENTS.md-primary with CLAUDE.md fallback, no dedicated file needed), matching my original label-only conclusion for those two.

Recording the shared near-miss for whoever revisits this: Antigravity's documentation surface is unusually noisy across secondary sources -- I initially pulled a DIFFERENT, more advanced .agents/agents.md persona-pipeline pattern from Antigravity's own codelab page and nearly reported that as the baseline convention; quest-cli separately hit contradictory 2026-dated third-party guides, one claiming AGENTS.md overrides GEMINI.md and another the reverse. The authoritative page is antigravity.google/docs/cli/best-practices/ -- go there directly, not a codelab or a blog.

IMPLEMENTED AND VERIFIED (2026-09-09). Widened the codex/AGENTS.md label to name pi, OpenCode, and cite the OpenCode product-surface exemption in code comments. Added a genuine NEW 'antigravity' target -> GEMINI.md (src/core/antigravity-bridge.ts + src/commands/antigravity-bridge.ts, mirroring the Hermes bridge exactly: plain nudge file, no skill directory, no credentials), gated on Bun.which('gemini') per detectAgentAvailability's existing one-representative-binary-per-option pattern (matches how codex's availability check already covers Cursor/Zed/Warp/Aider/RooCode without checking each separately). Coordinated final wording with quest-cli throughout (both AGENTS.md and GEMINI.md label text match theirs where the option sets overlap). Confirmed lore agents (non-interactive, flag-driven, regenerates only already-configured bridges) is unaffected by construction -- no multiselect concept there, matching quest's explicit instructions/--update-instructions single-target decision.

New unit tests: --antigravity writes only GEMINI.md not AGENTS.md, protects an existing GEMINI.md, wizard offers antigravity only when gemini is detected with the correct dual-tool label, and the widened AGENTS.md label names pi and OpenCode. Full suite 2893 pass/1 skip/0 fail (4 new tests), lint/typecheck/lore check all clean.

PTY-verified twice in a real terminal: (1) no gemini binary -> antigravity correctly absent from the multiselect, widened AGENTS.md label renders correctly; (2) fake gemini binary added to PATH -> all four options render, GEMINI.md toggles on/off correctly, confirming writes ONLY GEMINI.md (verified file content and absence of AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md on disk), full run to completion with exit 0.

CHANGELOG.md's [Unreleased] also corrected: the existing multi-select entry from PR #629 still said 'every one pre-checked by default', stale since PR #630 reversed that default -- fixed in the same commit rather than left to compound.
